Case A

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are its author. That behavior is covered, and the README describes it.

Nothing in the change blocks merging, but merging waits on the required unit test check. That check is still running on the commit being reviewed after the 15-minute watch ended, and nothing has failed.

I recommend deliver because the unit test check is still running and one more watch can see it finish.

Pick one:
1. deliver - continue by watching the checks for one more 15-minute window, without adding repair or sync attempts. [recommended]
2. assess - stop delivery and post nothing, because there are no problems to report.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are its author. That behavior is covered, and the README describes it.

Nothing in the change blocks merging, and the required unit test and image build checks passed. GitHub won't let this merge until a reviewer other than you approves it, and your write access gives you no admin override. No repair, branch update, watch or workflow approval can supply that review.

I recommend stop because merging needs an approving review from someone other than you, and nothing offered here can provide it.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is. [recommended]
2. deliver - only after another reviewer approves, continue delivery with 10 more repair attempts and 10 more base-branch updates allowed.
3. assess - stop delivery and post nothing, because there are no problems to report.

Case C

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=1

Merging waits on the required unit test job, which cannot start until a repository maintainer approves its workflow run. This is the same missing approval that stopped the last attempt, and the repair attempts allowed for this run are used up. Approving the workflow run needs maintainer permission that you do not have.

I recommend stop because the unit test job stays blocked until a maintainer approves its workflow run, and nothing offered here can supply that approval.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is. [recommended]
2. deliver - continue with 10 more repair attempts and 10 more base-branch updates allowed, but it stops again until a maintainer approves the workflow run.

Case D

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are its author. The README describes that behavior, but the endpoint does not return the build version yet, so that requirement is not covered.

One problem blocks merging. The health endpoint returns a fixed version string instead of the build version, so a deployed build reports the wrong version (src/health.ts:8). The local test health_version in tests/health.test.mjs fails because of it. A drafted repair makes the endpoint read the existing build-version value.

I recommend deliver because this is your PR and the drafted repair fixes the problem without needing anyone else's decision.

Pick one:
1. deliver - repair blockers, rebase on main, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review and make no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

Case E

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR by robin makes the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are a requested reviewer. That behavior is covered, and the README describes it.

One problem blocks merging. The description says the endpoint "Reports uptime", but it returns only the build version, which would mislead anyone relying on the description (src/health.ts:8).
Proposed description fix: "Reports uptime" -> "Reports the build version"

I recommend deliver because the drafted description correction fixes the only problem and needs no decision from the author.

Pick one:
1. deliver - apply the drafted description correction, merge main into the branch if it falls behind, watch the checks, and continue until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review and make no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR by robin aims to make the health endpoint respond with the build version, and you are a requested reviewer. The endpoint does not return a version field, so that requirement is not covered.

One problem blocks merging. The health response has no version field, so callers cannot tell which build is running (src/health.ts:8). The local test health_version in tests/health.test.mjs fails because of it. Delivery is unavailable because you only have read access and cannot push to this PR's branch.

I recommend assess because posting the problem gives robin the concrete fix, and you cannot push a repair yourself.

Pick one:
1. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review and make no repairs. [recommended]
2. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Case G

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/contract-exception recommended=1

The pending proposal would change the approved spec so the build version is served at /status instead of /health.

I recommend preserve contract because the existing /health handler can return the same build version without changing the spec.

Pick one:
1. preserve contract - keep /health as the required endpoint, drop the proposed spec change, and continue the repair so /health returns the build version. [recommended]
2. accept contract change - amend the approved spec so the build version is served at /status, then continue delivery.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.
